criterion.metric: profile likelihood barrier depth, straight line in chart coordinates
criterion.floor_reference: 0.5 * B_certified log-units, the cost of a curve one noise unit away at every bias
criterion.null_control: the same criterion over the same number of ordinary prior draws that form no witness pair, taken in draw order

decision.floor_barrier: 0.5 * B_certified log-units, inherited unchanged from BarrierCriterion
decision.classifier: RIDGE if at least ridge_fraction of witness pairs are at or below the floor barrier; BASIN if none is; MIXED otherwise
decision.matched_cell: chart L, d=16 -- matched in d to chart J, matched in interpolant family to chart G
decision.if_matched_cell_is_ridge: chart effect: two charts at one d disagree
decision.if_matched_cell_is_basin: dimension effect: both d=16 cells are basins and the only ridge is d=4
decision.if_matched_cell_is_mixed: neither; one more cell was not enough
decision.rulings_stated_falsifier: chart L d=16 sits at the floor like chart G d=4, which would make the ridge/basin split a dimension effect rather than a chart effect
decision.why_inverted: chart L at the floor while chart J at the same d is not means two charts at one dimension disagree, and d=4 and d=16 land on the same side; that is a chart effect. The dimension reading requires chart L to behave like chart J, not like chart G.
decision.reproduction_control: chart G d=4 and chart J d=16 are re-measured here through the same imported function; their barrier medians must reproduce generation 9's

rule.barriers_are: generation 9's BarrierCriterion, imported unchanged, at the production grid N=301 -- the criterion outputs/g10/ridge_basin.json was measured under
rule.recompute_through: run_g10._barrier_set, imported; the same function that produced outputs/g10/ridge_basin.json
rule.refinement_changes: which pairs are counted, and nothing else
rule.reproduction_control: the full 37-pair set is re-measured first and every per-pair depth must reproduce outputs/g10/ridge_basin.json bit-identically. A recount over depths that do not reproduce is a new measurement wearing the old one's name
rule.counted_set: the pairs that survive the battery, in their committed order
rule.null_control: as in run_g10._barrier_set: consecutive non-witness draws taken in draw order, one per counted witness pair. A smaller counted set takes a prefix of the same ordered list, so the null is not re-drawn
rule.classifier: run_g10.classify against RidgeBasinDecision, unchanged: RIDGE if at least ridge_fraction of counted pairs are at or below the floor barrier, BASIN if none is, MIXED otherwise
rule.the_barrier_is_an_upper_bound: BOUND-01 and PATH-01, carried rather than re-derived. Every depth is the barrier along a STRAIGHT LINE in this chart's own coordinates, so it is an UPPER bound and a shallower path may exist. For chart L this direction is the unfavourable one: a basin statement rests on finding NO path below the floor, and an upper bound cannot establish that none exists. Refinement does not repair this and is not claimed to
rule.what_is_not_recomputed: chart G and chart J. Their sets are untouched, so their numbers stand and the three-set comparison stays one measurement rather than two spliced together

path_lengths.note: descriptive context for the barrier depths, not part of the registered classifier: the barrier walks a straight line in this chart's coordinates, so a set whose pairs are further apart has longer lines

reproduction_control_B1.why: the full 37-pair set is re-measured first and every per-pair depth must reproduce outputs/g10/ridge_basin.json bit-identically. A recount over depths that do not reproduce is a new measurement wearing the old one's name

self_consistency_S1.why: the same pair walked twice by a deterministic function must give the same depth; if it does not, the counted set is not a subset of the full one

verdict.reading: chart L stays a basin and gains its coverage. Spine items 3 and 4 keep their classification and WIT-02 becomes satisfied on all three committed sets, which is what ladder rung L1 requires. The basin remains a SEARCH statement against an upper-bound barrier -- refinement tests the witnesses, not the connectivity -- and the minimum-energy path is still not computed
